questions.stem: A heuristic is admissible when h(n) ≤ h∗(n) for every node n, where h∗ is the true cost. Which statement says h is NOT admissible?
options: Every node n has h(n) > h∗(n)
Some node n has h(n) ≤ h∗(n)
No node n has h(n) > h∗(n)
Some node n has h(n) > h∗(n)
questions.explain: The negation of "for every n, h(n) ≤ h∗(n)" is "for some n, h(n) > h∗(n)". One bad node is enough.

questions.stem:
What does this program print?

```python
g = [0, 2, 5]
h = [6, 3, 1]
print(min(g[i] + h[i] for i in range(3)))
```
questions.explain: The sums g[i] + h[i] are 6, 5 and 6, and the minimum is 5.

questions.stem: Uniform-cost search always expands the frontier node with the smallest value of which quantity?
options: Estimated cost h to the goal
Number of edges from the start
Path cost g from the start
questions.explain: Uniform-cost search orders the frontier by g, the total path cost so far. Ordering by edge count is BFS.

questions.stem: The explored set is E = {S, A, B} and the frontier is F = {B, C}. How many distinct nodes are in E ∪ F?
questions.explain: E ∪ F = {S, A, B, C}. The shared node B is counted once.
